summary: How long the owner must take care of a bechor before giving it to the Kohen, and that a bechor should be eaten within its first year.

chunks.he: עַד כַּמָּה יִשְׂרָאֵל חַיָּבִים לְהִטַּפֵּל בַּבְּכוֹר.
chunks.en: How long must a Yisrael take care of a bechor?
chunks.st: Until when must an Israelite tend to and raise a firstborn animal before giving it to the priest?

chunks.en: For a small animal,
chunks.st: With regard to a small animal, e.g., a sheep or goat, it is

chunks.en: thirty days,
chunks.st: thirty days,

chunks.en: and for a big animal, fifty days.
chunks.st: and with regard to a large animal, e.g., cattle, it is fifty days.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: for a small animal, three months.
chunks.st: With regard to a small animal, it is three months.

chunks.he: אָמַר לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן בְּתוֹךְ זְמַן זֶה
chunks.en: If the Kohen said to him during this time,
chunks.st: If the priest said to the owner within that period:

chunks.en: "Give it to me,"
chunks.st: Give it to me,

chunks.en: he should not give it to him.
chunks.st: that owner may not give it to him.

chunks.en: If it had a blemish,
chunks.st: And if it is a blemished firstborn

chunks.he: אָמַר לוֹ תֶּן לִי שֶׁאוֹכְלֶנּוּ, מֻתָּר.
chunks.en: and the Kohen said, "Give it to me so I can eat it," it is allowed.
chunks.st: and the priest said to him: Give it to me so I may eat it, it is permitted for the owner to give it to him.

chunks.en: And when the Beis HaMikdash stands,
chunks.st: And at the time that the Temple is standing,

chunks.en: if it had no blemish,
chunks.st: if it is unblemished

chunks.he: אָמַר לוֹ תֶּן לִי שֶׁאַקְרִיבֶנּוּ, מֻתָּר.
chunks.en: and the Kohen said, "Give it to me so I can bring it as a korban," it is allowed.
chunks.st: and the priest said to him: Give it to me and I will sacrifice it, it is permitted for the owner to give it to him.

chunks.en: A bechor is eaten year by year,
chunks.st: The firstborn animal is eaten year by year, i.e., within its first year,

chunks.en: whether it has no blemish or has a blemish,
chunks.st: whether it is blemished or whether it is unblemished,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.he: לִפְנֵי ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ תֹאכְלֶנּוּ שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה:
chunks.en: "Before Hashem your G-d you shall eat it, year by year."
chunks.st: “You shall eat it before the Lord your God year by year” (Deuteronomy 15:20).

summary: If a bechor gets a blemish in its first year, the owner may keep it for the whole year. After that, he may keep it for only thirty days.

chunks.en: If it got a blemish during its first year,
chunks.st: If a blemish developed within its first year,

chunks.he: מֻתָּר לְקַיְּמוֹ כָּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ.
chunks.en: he may keep it for the whole twelve months.
chunks.st: it is permitted for the owner to maintain the animal for the entire twelve months.

chunks.en: After its first year,
chunks.st: If a blemish developed after twelve months have passed,

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּמוֹ אֶלָּא עַד שְׁלשִׁים יוֹם:
chunks.en: he may keep it for only thirty days.
chunks.st: it is permitted for the owner to maintain the animal for only thirty days.

summary: Someone shechted a bechor first and only then showed its blemish to an expert. The Rabbis argue if it is allowed.

chunks.en: Someone who shechts a bechor and then shows its blemish:
chunks.st: In the case of one who slaughters the firstborn animal and only then shows its blemish
chunks.stMore: to an expert to determine whether it is a blemish, and it was established by the expert that it is in fact a blemish that renders its slaughter permitted,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah allows it.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda deems it permitted
chunks.stMore: for a priest to derive benefit from the firstborn.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: since it was shechted not
chunks.st: Since it was slaughtered not

chunks.en: by the word of an expert, it is forbidden.
chunks.st: according to the ruling of an expert, it is prohibited.

summary: If someone who is not an expert lets a bechor be shechted by mistake, he must pay. A judge who is an expert does not pay for a mistake, as we see from a story with Rabbi Tarfon.

chunks.en: Someone who is not an expert
chunks.st: In a case involving one who is not an expert,

chunks.he: וְרָאָה אֶת הַבְּכוֹר וְנִשְׁחַט עַל פִּיו,
chunks.en: looked at a bechor, and it was shechted because of what he said:
chunks.st: and he examined the firstborn animal and it was slaughtered on the basis of his ruling,

chunks.en: it must be buried,
chunks.st: that animal must be buried, and the non-expert

chunks.en: and he must pay from his own pocket.
chunks.st: must pay compensation to the priest from his property.

chunks.en: A judge who judged a case
chunks.st: Apropos the previous mishna,

chunks.he: זִכָּה אֶת הַחַיָּב וְחִיֵּב אֶת הַזַּכַּאי,
chunks.en: and freed the guilty one and made the innocent one guilty,
chunks.st: which taught that a judge

chunks.he: טִמֵּא אֶת הַטָהוֹר וְטִהֵר אֶת הַטָּמֵא,
chunks.en: or said something tahor was tamei, or something tamei was tahor:
chunks.st: who was an expert for the court

chunks.en: what he did is done, and he must pay from his own pocket.
chunks.st: and who erred

chunks.he: וְאִם הָיָה מֻמְחֶה לְבֵית דִּין, פָּטוּר מִלְּשַׁלֵּם.
chunks.en: But if he was an expert for the beis din, he does not have to pay.
chunks.st: is exempt from payment, this mishna teaches:

chunks.en: Once there was a cow whose womb was taken out.
chunks.st: There was an incident involving a cow whose womb was removed,
chunks.stMore: and when Rabbi Tarfon was consulted he ruled that it is an animal with a wound that will cause it to die within twelve months [tereifa], which is forbidden for consumption.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon said it was treif, and fed it to the dogs.
chunks.st: And based on the ruling of Rabbi Tarfon, the questioner fed it to the dogs.

chunks.en: The case came before the Sages, and they allowed it.
chunks.st: And the incident came before the Sages of the court in Yavne, and they ruled that such an animal is permitted and is not a tereifa.

chunks.en: Todos the doctor said,
chunks.st: And Theodosius [Todos] the doctor said:

chunks.en: "No cow or pig leaves
chunks.st: A cow or pig does not emerge

chunks.he: מֵאֲלֶכְּסַנְדְּרִיָּא עַד שֶׁהֵם חוֹתְכִין אֶת הָאֵם שֶׁלָּהּ,
chunks.en: Alexandria until they cut out its womb,
chunks.st: from Alexandria of Egypt unless the residents sever its womb

chunks.en: so that it will not have babies."
chunks.st: so that it will not give birth
chunks.stMore: in the future. The breeds of cows and pigs in Alexandria were of exceptional quality and the people of Alexandria did not want them reproduced elsewhere. The fact that these animals lived long lives after their wombs were removed proves that the hysterectomy did not render them tereifot. Upon hearing this,

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon said:

chunks.en: "Your donkey is gone, Tarfon!"
chunks.st: Your donkey is gone, Tarfon,
chunks.stMore: as he believed he was required to compensate the owner for the cow that he ruled to be a tereifa.

words.note: He thought he would have to sell his donkey to pay back the owner.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said to him:

chunks.en: "Rabbi Tarfon, you do not have to pay,
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon, you are

chunks.en: because you are an expert for the beis din,
chunks.st: an expert for the court,

chunks.he: וְכָל הַמֻּמְחֶה לְבֵית דִּין פָּטוּר מִלְּשַׁלֵּם:
chunks.en: and any expert for the beis din does not have to pay."
chunks.st: and any expert for the court is exempt from liability to pay.

summary: A person who takes pay to check a bechor for blemishes may not be relied on, unless he is a great expert like Ila in Yavneh.

chunks.en: Someone who takes pay to check a bechor for blemishes:
chunks.st: In the case of an individual who takes payment to be one who examines firstborn
chunks.stMore: animals to determine whether they are blemished,

chunks.en: we do not shecht because of what he says,
chunks.st: one may not slaughter the firstborn on the basis of his ruling,

chunks.he: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיָה מֻמְחֶה כְּאִילָא בְיַבְנֶה,
chunks.en: unless he was an expert like Ila in Yavneh,
chunks.st: unless he was an expert like Ila in Yavne,

chunks.en: whom the Sages allowed to take
chunks.st: whom the Sages in Yavne permitted to take a wage of

chunks.en: four issar for a small animal
chunks.st: four issar for issuing a ruling concerning a small animal

chunks.en: and six for a big one,
chunks.st: and six issar for issuing a ruling concerning a large animal.

chunks.en: whether it had no blemish or had a blemish.
chunks.st: They permitted this provided that he would be paid whether it turned out that the firstborn was unblemished or whether it was blemished.

summary: A judge or witness who takes pay for judging or testifying is not counted. But he may be paid for the work he missed, like a worker.

chunks.en: Someone who takes pay to judge:
chunks.st: In the case of one who takes his wages to judge cases,

chunks.en: his judgments do not count.
chunks.st: his rulings are void. In the case of one who takes wages

chunks.en: To be a witness: what he says does not count.
chunks.st: to testify, his testimonies are void.

chunks.en: To sprinkle the parah adumah water, or to make it,
chunks.st: With regard to one who takes wages to sprinkle the purification waters of the red heifer upon one who contracted impurity imparted by a corpse, and one who takes wages to sanctify those waters,

chunks.he: מֵימָיו מֵי מְעָרָה וְאֶפְרוֹ אֵפֶר מִקְלֶה.
chunks.en: his water is plain cave water, and his ashes are plain burnt ashes.
chunks.st: the halakhic status of his water is that of cave water, and the status of his ashes is that of mere burnt ashes.

chunks.en: If he was a Kohen and he made him tamei so he could not eat his terumah,
chunks.st: Although taking actual wages is prohibited, if the one examining the firstborn, or the judge, or the witness, was a priest, and the one who requires his services rendered him impure and prevented him from partaking of his teruma,

chunks.en: he must give him food, drink and oil to rub on.
chunks.st: that person must provide the priest with food, drink, and oil for smearing on his body from his own non-sacred property.

chunks.en: If he was old,
chunks.st: And likewise if the one examining the firstborn, or the judge, or the witness, was an elderly person,

chunks.en: he lets him ride on a donkey,
chunks.st: the one who requires his services transports him on a donkey.

chunks.en: and he pays him like a worker.
chunks.st: And in all these cases, although it is prohibited to take wages, the one who requires his services gives him his wages like the wages of a laborer,
chunks.stMore: as he was unable to perform his usual labor that day.

words.note: Paid only for the work he missed, not for judging.

summary: If a person is suspected of selling bechor meat, we must be careful about what we buy from him.

chunks.en: Someone suspected about bechoros:
chunks.st: In the case of one who is suspect with regard to firstborn
chunks.stMore: animals of slaughtering them and selling their meat when it is prohibited to do so,

chunks.en: we do not buy from him even deer meat,
chunks.st: one may neither purchase meat from him, including even deer meat,

chunks.en: nor hides that are not tanned.
chunks.st: nor may one purchase from him hides that are not tanned.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: we may buy from him hides of female animals.
chunks.st: One may purchase hides of female animals from him,
chunks.stMore: as the halakhot of firstborn animals are in effect only with regard to males.

chunks.he: וְאֵין לוֹקְחִין מִמֶּנּוּ צֶמֶר מְלֻּבָּן וְצוֹאִי,
chunks.en: We do not buy from him clean or dirty wool,
chunks.st: And one may not purchase bleached or dirty wool from him.

chunks.en: but we may buy from him thread and clothing.
chunks.st: But one may purchase spun thread from him, and all the more so may one purchase garments from him.

summary: If a person is suspected of not keeping shemittah, we do not buy flax from him, but we may buy thread or cloth.

chunks.en: Someone suspected about shemittah:
chunks.st: In the case of one who is suspect with regard to the Sabbatical
chunks.stMore: Year, i.e., of sowing or engaging in commerce with Sabbatical-Year produce,

words.note: The seventh year, when the land rests.

chunks.he: אֵין לוֹקְחִין מִמֶּנּוּ פִשְׁתָּן וַאֲפִלּוּ סֶרֶק,
chunks.en: we do not buy flax from him, not even combed flax,
chunks.st: one may not purchase flax from him, and this applies even to combed
chunks.stMore: flax, in which much labor and exertion was invested.

chunks.en: but we may buy from him thread and woven cloth.
chunks.st: But one may purchase spun thread and woven fabric from such individuals.

summary: If a person is suspected of selling terumah as plain food, the Rabbis argue what we may still buy from him.

chunks.he: הֶחָשׁוּד לִהְיוֹת מוֹכֵר תְּרוּמָה לְשֵׁם חֻלִּין,
chunks.en: Someone suspected of selling terumah as regular food:
chunks.st: In the case of one who is suspect with regard to selling teruma under the guise of non-sacred produce,

chunks.he: אֵין לוֹקְחִין מִמֶּנּוּ אֲפִלּוּ מַיִם אוֹ מֶלַח,
chunks.en: we do not buy from him even water or salt.
chunks.st: one may not purchase even water and salt from him; this is

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Yehudah says.
chunks.st: the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.he: כּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ זִקַּת תְּרוּמוֹת וּמַעַשְׂרוֹת,
chunks.en: anything that has terumah and ma'aser
chunks.st: One may not purchase from him any item that has relevance to teruma and tithes.

chunks.en: we do not buy from him.
chunks.st: However, one may purchase water and salt from him, as teruma and tithes do not apply to them.

summary: Someone suspected of breaking one mitzvah is not suspected of breaking a different one. A person suspected of a thing may not judge or be a witness about it.

chunks.en: Someone suspected about shemittah
chunks.st: One who is suspect with regard to the Sabbatical Year

chunks.en: is not suspected about ma'aser.
chunks.st: is not suspect with regard to tithes; and likewise,

chunks.en: Someone suspected about ma'aser
chunks.st: one who is suspect with regard to tithes

chunks.en: is not suspected about shemittah.
chunks.st: is not suspect with regard to the Sabbatical Year.

chunks.en: Someone suspected about this or that
chunks.st: One who is suspect with regard to this, the Sabbatical Year, or with regard to that, tithes,

chunks.en: is suspected about taharah, keeping things tahor.
chunks.st: is suspect with regard to selling ritually impure foods as though they were ritually pure items.

chunks.en: And some people are suspected about taharah
chunks.st: But there are those who are suspect with regard to ritually pure items

chunks.en: but are not suspected
chunks.st: who are not suspect with regard to this, the Sabbatical Year,

chunks.en: about this or that.
chunks.st: nor with regard to that, tithes.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle with regard to these matters:

chunks.en: anyone who is suspected about something
chunks.st: Anyone who is suspect with regard to a specific matter

chunks.en: may not judge it and may not be a witness about it.
chunks.st: may neither adjudicate cases nor testify in cases involving that matter.
